STEP 1 - Scene: A snack of raw almonds on a small white paper plate, photographed from directly overhead.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a paper plate with a rim, probably about 18 cm across. In the image it spans about 265 px, so 1 cm is roughly 14.7 px. An almond is about 40 px long, which is about 2.7 cm. That is plausible for an almond, which is usually 2.2-2.5 cm. Plate area is 3.14 x 9² ≈ 254 cm². The flat inner part is smaller.

STEP 3 - Items: Whole almonds only.

STEP 4 - Area: The pile spans about 160 px, or roughly 11 cm. Its area is about 95 cm², which is about 37% of the plate. Almonds are not packed completely, so I use about 35%.

STEP 5 - Volume: The pile is roughly 1.5-2 cm high. 90 cm² x 1.8 cm ≈ 160 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole almonds have a bulk density of about 0.6 g/ml, because there are gaps between them. 160 x 0.6 ≈ 96 g. As a check, I count about 45 almonds at roughly 1.2 g each, which gives about 54 g. I take a figure between the two, about 65 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Almonds are about 580 kcal per 100 g, so 65 g gives about 377 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A small plate with a single layer of nuts, partly two layers deep, holding about 45-50 almonds at about 65 g is plausible.
